Aholah--</hi>that is, "Her tent" (put for worship, as the first worship of God in Israel was in a tent or tabernacle), as contrasted with Aholibah, that is, "My tent in her." The Beth-el worship of Samaria was of her own devising, not of God's appointment; the temple-worship of Jerusalem was expressly appointed by Jehovah, who "dwelt" there, "setting up His tabernacle among the people as His" (<reference osisRef="Exod.25.8">Ex 25:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.26.11">Le 26:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.26.12">12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.22.19">Jos 22:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.76.2">Psa 76:2</reference>).<div eID="gen20675" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20676" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the elder--</hi>Samaria is called "the elder" because she preceded Judah in her apostasy and its punishment.<div eID="gen20676" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20677" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they were mine--</hi>Previous to apostasy under Jeroboam, Samaria (Israel, or the ten tribes), equally with Judah, worshipped the true God. God therefore never renounced the right over Israel, but sent prophets, as Elijah and Elisha, to declare His will to them. <div eID="gen20677" type="x-p"/>

God therefore never renounced the right over Israel, but sent prophets, as Elijah and Elisha, to declare His will to them.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11423"/><div sID="gen20678" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11423"/><hi type="bold">5. when ... mine--</hi>literally, "under Me," that is, subject to Me as her lawful husband.<div eID="gen20678" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20679" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">neighbours--</hi>On the northeast the kingdom of Israel bordered on that of Assyria; for the latter had occupied much of Syria. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11434"/><div sID="gen20695" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11434"/><hi type="bold">16. sent messengers ... into Chaldea--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.29">Eze 16:29</reference>). It was she that solicited the Chaldeans, not they her. Probably the occasion was when Judah sought to strengthen herself by a Chaldean alliance against a menaced attack by Egypt (compare 2Ki 23:29-35; 24:1-7). God made the object of their sinful desire the instrument of their punishment. Jehoiakim, probably by a stipulation of tribute, enlisted Nebuchadnezzar against Pharaoh, whose tributary he previously had been; failing to keep his stipulation, he brought on himself Nebuchadnezzar's vengeance. <div eID="gen20695" type="x-p"/>

Koa, "rich ... princely."<div eID="gen20706" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20707" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">desirable young men--</hi>strong irony.
